correctness.rationale: For n>=3, the crown graph has distance 1 between nonpaired opposite-shore vertices, 2 within a shore, and 3 across the missing matched edge. For each omitted a_i, the selected-vertex distance multiset has n-x copies of 2 and, depending on i in Y, either n-y copies of 1 or n-y-1 copies of 1 plus one 3; the symmetric expression holds for b_j. Each shore therefore admits at most two omissions, and two require exactly one mate omitted across the shore. When x=y=1 the two omitted vertices have identical multisets; when x=y=2, the required intersection=1 also produces a cross-shore collision. Different x,y give different 2-counts, leaving precisely (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(2,1),(1,2), with the latter requiring intersection=1. Counting omitted indexed pairs gives odim(Cr_n)=2n-3, 2n(n-1) bases and the exact three-term set enumerator. Independently implemented exhaustive graph-distance/subset checks n=3,4,5,6 confirmed all cases, including the absent size 2n-2;  finite checks do not prove the infinite theorem.
